title: Midlife Registered Dietitian (Contract) - Licensed in Pennsylvania
description:
About us

Pomelo Care is the leading virtual medical practice for women and children, providing care across pregnancy, postpartum, pediatrics, menopause, and perimenopause. We combine proactive, 24/7 clinical care with technology that helps us reach patients earlier, identify risks sooner, and deliver personalized care throughout their journey. Our team includes clinicians, technologists, operators, and problem-solvers working together to make high-quality care more accessible for families nationwide.

We’re building a network of experienced registered dietitians to deliver synchronous patient visits for individuals navigating midlife, perimenopause, and menopause transitions.

This is a 1099 independent contractor role and is not an employment (W-2) position. As an independent contractor, you will not be eligible for employee benefits, including but not limited to health insurance, paid time off, workers’ compensation, or unemployment benefits. Pomelo Care will provide services to support your independent practice, such as client matching, billing and administrative support.

As part of the Pomelo network, you will:

  • Conduct synchronous video visits with patients navigating midlife, perimenopause, and menopause transitions
  • Provide one-on-one virtual nutrition care via phone and video calls to facilitate lifestyle change and enhance patients’ wellbeing
  • Work closely with patients in a multi-week program format to support symptom improvement and sustained behavior change in patients experiencing perimenopause
  • Maintain timely and accurate documentation
  • Follow applicable clinical, documentation, privacy, quality, and compliance standards for visits conducted through Pomelo

To join Pomelo’s growing network, you are/have:

  • National certification as a registered dietitian (RD) or registered dietitian/nutritionist (RDN) with license to practice in Pennsylvania
  • A minimum of 3 years of experience providing providing evidence-based nutrition therapy for patients with:
    • Conditions of metabolic syndrome
    • Weight loss and body composition changes
    • Osteopenia/osteoporosis
    • Gut health concerns, including bloating, IBS, and elimination diets
    • Plant-forward/plant-based diets and anti-inflammatory eating patterns
  • Comfortable using telehealth platforms, video conferencing tools, and electronic documentation systems
  • Strong clinical judgment with the ability to work independently during patient visits

Credentialing process & next steps:

Once you apply, our team will guide you through the credentialing process, which includes:

  • Meeting with someone from our recruitment & clinical teams for 2-30-minute video calls
  • Providing proof/verification of licensure & personal liability insurance
  • Enrolling with commercial health plans through Pomelo
  • Completing a background screening

Support for your midlife practice:

By joining Pomelo, we will provide the support you need to focus on what you do best – caring for families.

  • Focus on Care, Not Paperwork: We handle credentialing, billing, and administrative support for visits conducted through Pomelo
  • Connect with Patients: We provide patient matching and scheduling support based on your availability, licensure, credentialing status, patient demand, and applicable payer or clinical requirements
  • Comprehensive Support: You’ll have access to administrative and technical support to navigate Pomelo’s systems, as well as documentation support for visits conducted through Pomelo
  • Clinical Community: You’ll have access to optional case consultations, optional provider forums, and optional clinical updates
  • Maintain Your Flexibility: You choose the days and times you make yourself available for Pomelo patient visits. You may accept or decline available visit opportunities, and Pomelo does not guarantee any minimum number of visits, patients, or compensation

At Pomelo, we are committed to hiring the best team to improve outcomes for all mothers and babies, regardless of their background. We need diverse perspectives to reflect the diversity of problems we face and the population we serve. We look to hire people from a variety of backgrounds, including but not limited to race, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, religion, disability, and veteran status.

Compensation

Dietitians are compensated on a per-visit basis. Rates may vary by visit type, visit length, visit timing, payer requirements, and other program factors. Pomelo does not guarantee a minimum number of visits or earnings. Based on current visit rates and typical visit lengths, completed visits may result in approximate earnings equivalent to $60.00 to $70.00 per active visit hour.

Potential Fraud Warning


Please be cautious of potential recruitment fraud. With the increase of remote work and digital hiring, phishing and job scams are on the rise with malicious actors impersonating real employees and sending fake job offers in an effort to collect personal or financial information.

Pomelo Care will never ask you to pay a fee or download software as part of the interview process with our company. Pomelo Care will also never ask for your personal banking or other financial information until after you have signed an offer of employment and completed onboarding paperwork that is provided by our People Operations team. All official communication with Pomelo Care People Operations team will come from domain email addresses ending in @pomelocare.com.

If you receive a message that seems suspicious, we encourage you to pause communication and contact us directly at careers@pomelocare.com to confirm its legitimacy. For your safety, we also recommend applying only through our official Careers page. If you believe you have been the victim of a scam or identity theft, please contact your local law enforcement agency or another trusted authority for guidance.

title: Success Coach Caseworker
description:
Title: Success Coach Caseworker

Full-Time Position

Status:
Non-Exempt

Supervisor: success coach supervisor

JFCS Pittsburgh

Since 1937, JFCS Pittsburgh has been pushing what’s possible in human services—combining compassion, innovation, and a relentless commitment to dignity and justice. We partner with people across the region to navigate life’s changes and challenges, ensuring that no neighbor has to navigate these difficulties alone.

We proudly serve job seekers, refugees and immigrants, individuals with disabilities, people experiencing food insecurity, those seeking mental health support, youth, and older adults. Through meaningful support and compassionate care, our goal is to help every person feel valued, empowered, and able to reach their full potential.

At JFCS, your work matters. You’ll join a team of passionate problem‑solvers and strategic thinkers who care deeply about people and aren’t afraid to rethink the way support is delivered. Here, creativity is encouraged, compassion drives every decision, and your impact is felt immediately in the community.

If you want your work to spark purpose, connection, and meaningful change—JFCS is where you can make it happen.

About the Program

This program is a new interdepartmental initiative that aims to provide support to individuals receiving services from JFCS. Through Success Coaches, individuals will help clients reduce barriers, build skills and confidence, and achieve stability that leads to economic mobility. With the help of Success Coaches, each enrolled participant will create a service plan with goals to address their circumstances and regular touch points to track progress.

Position Summary

JFCS Success Coaches work with individuals from diverse backgrounds and needs to identify barriers that limit their ability to achieve their goals. Success coaches expand what clients can see, what they believe is possible, and what they are equipped to do.

Depending on client need, Success Coaches may engage in an intensive, urgent response to a crisis, or may provide resources to clients struggling to solve life’s challenges on their own. Success Coaches work with the client to prioritize their goals as they navigate the barriers on their pathway to stability and success.

A limited number of participants in JFCS career preparation and support programs who meet program eligibility requirements may receive a stipend for up to 18 months through the Catalyst for Economic Mobility. This stipend would allow them to achieve greater financial stability as they build toward the future. Success Coaches will guide these participants in the Catalyst for Economic Mobility through “light touch” support and barrier reduction, in addition to support with goal setting and resource navigation.

If you are driven by genuine respect for people struggling to overcome barriers to their own success, and you find meaning in partnering with clients to find solutions to barriers, this work is for you.

Duties and Responsibilities

Client Services & Coaching

  • Conduct intake sessions to assess client needs across various domains: housing, food, childcare, transportation, income, healthcare, technology, and financial assets.
  • Co-create individualized service plans with clients, including measurable action items that are primarily assigned to and owned by the client.
  • Provide light-touch follow-up to review goal achievement and engage in intentional conversations with clients.
  • Conduct warm referrals to community resources, financial coaching programs, workforce development services, and other supports identified collaboratively with the client.
  • Provide specific support, monitoring, and coordination for participants enrolled in the Catalyst for Economic Mobility.

Resource Navigation

  • Maintain current working knowledge of local community resources related to housing, food assistance, childcare, transportation, financial assistance, workforce development, and healthcare and other emerging needs.
  • Verify resource eligibility requirements, waitlist status, and geographic availability prior to making referrals.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with community partners and referral agencies to facilitate warm, effective connections.
  • Support clients in navigating applications and systems when structural barriers require direct caseworker assistance.
  • Follow up as needed for all support provided

Training

  • Actively participate in training to develop coaching skills and strength-based models, such as motivational interviewing, to help clients identify and use skills and resources that support behavioral changes leading to economic mobility.
  • Workshop development and presentations for client cohorts

Documentation & Program Compliance

  • Maintain timely and accurate case notes in the program’s case management system.
  • Document service plans, action items, referrals, and session progress in accordance with program standards.
  • Complete required program data entry to support outcome tracking, reporting, and funder compliance.
  • Participate in regular supervision, team meetings, case consultations, and professional development activities.
  • Maintain confidentiality and adhere to all ethical standards, data privacy requirements, and mandatory reporting laws.

Qualifications

  • Creativity, innovation, curiosity, and patience are essential skills.
  • Must have excellent English (spoken and written)
  • Top-level organizational and communication skills
  • The ability to work under strict deadlines
  • Comfort with inputting information into data systems.
  • Must work well as part of a team
  • Must be sensitive to cultural differences of clients and staff from diverse background
  • Able to work flexible hours.
  • Access to a vehicle is required.
  • Bachelor’s Degree a plus.

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Must be able to lift up to 25 pounds at times.

title: IT Program Project Delivery, Off
description:

State Street Investment Management is looking for a senior Business Analyst, officer for our China office, as part of the Information Technology organization.

This position will be responsible for leading business analysis and driving solution delivery for investment management applications and platforms, working closely with global business stakeholders and technology teams. The role requires the ability to operate with a high degree of independence, own workstreams end to end, and translate business priorities into clear requirements, delivery plans, and implementation outcomes that improve operational efficiency and support risk and control standards.

The candidate should have working knowledge of asset management business and applications, with exposure to areas such as Content management systems, Product information systems, Marketing and Sales applications, workflow applications.

Our Information Technology function is vital to State Street Investment Management and is a key enabler for delivering data, insights, and digital capabilities to our clients. We continue to modernize our technology platforms and enhance business capabilities through cloud adoption, data analytics, and automation initiatives.

This role plays an important part in ensuring that business requirements are well understood, clearly defined, and effectively delivered, enabling scalable and high‑quality solutions that support business growth and operational excellence.

We offer a collaborative, global environment where business analysis skills are valued, and where individuals can grow their expertise by working on real business challenges in the asset management industry.

  • Experience leading requirement analysis, documentation, testing coordination, and delivery support for business or IT initiatives, with the ability to drive progress independently across multiple stakeholders.

  • Good written and verbal English communication skills.

Where will the role be based

The role will be based in Hangzhou, China.

About State Street

What we do. State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation, we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. State Street Investment Management is the asset management arm of State Street, serving clients to achieve their long-term investment goals through index, active, ETF and multi-asset class solutions.

Work, Live and Grow. We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. title: Senior Offensive Security Engineer
description:
Array is a financial innovation platform that helps digital brands, financial institutions, and fintechs get compelling consumer products to market faster. We deliver a suite of credit and identity monitoring tools, privacy protection, and a financial ads marketplace via embeddable widgets or a clean, modern API. Our private label offerings help drive revenue and increase engagement for our customers while empowering millions of consumers to achieve their financial goals.

As a remote-first company, we’re focused on providing opportunities for high performing individuals to have deep impact in the fast growing fintech space. A clear mission, a commitment to continuous improvement and a willingness to experiment empower us individually and together deliver the best products for our clients and users.

We're looking for an Offensive Security Engineer to think like an attacker and validate the security of Array's products through real-world exploitation. You’re a paid hacker; you'll operate with full access to our applications, source code, and infrastructure to identify vulnerabilities that create meaningful business risk—not theoretical findings. AI should be one of your primary tools, enabling you to analyze large codebases, accelerate hypothesis generation, and increase testing coverage while relying on your own judgment to validate results.

You Have:

  • 5+ years of offensive security, application security, penetration testing, or red team experience with a track record of finding real application vulnerabilities.
  • Deep expertise in modern web applications, APIs, authentication, authorization, distributed systems, and the OWASP Top 10.
  • Experience developing proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate real business impact, not just theoretical risk.
  • Proficiency using AI to accelerate vulnerability discovery, exploit development, code analysis, and security research while validating AI-generated output.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex vulnerabilities, attack paths, and remediation guidance to engineering teams.
  • A belief that AI is reshaping work, you instinctively use it to accelerate everything you do.

You Will:

  • Identify, validate, and demonstrate realistic attack paths against Array's products, infrastructure, and internal systems with a focus on business impact.
  • Analyze large, multi-language codebases using AI and manual techniques to uncover vulnerabilities, generate exploit hypotheses, and perform variant analysis.
  • Build safe proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate unauthorized access, privilege escalation, data exposure, business logic flaws, or other meaningful security risks.
  • Partner with engineering to validate remediations, confirm exploit paths are fully eliminated, and identify similar patterns elsewhere in the environment.
  • Document findings with clear evidence, technical root cause, business impact, and practical remediation guidance while continuously improving Array's offensive security capabilities.
  • Maintain a habit of using AI tools to think, build, and ship faster—it’s your default, not an afterthought.

Success Looks Like:

  • Demonstrated exploit paths to sensitive data, unauthorized access, or privilege escalation.
  • Security gaps identified that were not detected by existing tools or processes.
  • High-confidence validation that engineering fixes eliminate vulnerabilities and related attack paths.
  • Meaningful system coverage supported by documented testing methodology, whether vulnerabilities are found or not.

title: Senior Product Manager, Mobile Ecosystem
description:
Swift Navigation is hiring. Let us introduce ourselves. Swift Navigation is changing the way we navigate and understand the world. Trusted by major automotive OEMs, global industrial giants, and tier-1 technology platforms, Swift’s precise positioning solutions deliver centimeter-accurate GNSS (GPS) positioning to millions of devices worldwide. Our cloud-based software enables safer driving, optimized last-mile delivery, and new possibilities for robotics and automated systems. We are now leveraging this proven foundation to fundamentally upgrade the global mobile landscape, bringing high-accuracy positioning natively to consumer smartphones, enterprise fleets, and mass-market mobile hardware.



The Role

As the Product Manager for the Mobile Ecosystem, you will own the product definition, roadmap, and ecosystem strategy required to scale Swift’s location capabilities across global mobile platforms.

Working in a tight triad alongside Business Development, Product Marketing, and Engineering you will focus on achieving product-market fit for early-stage mobile initiatives. Your mission is to drive our technology into native, device-level integrations that easily scale across hardware lines.



Key Responsibilities

  • Native Integration Roadmap: Define product requirements for native, device-level activation of Swift’s positioning services via standard mobile operating system location APIs.
  • Ecosystem Alignment: Partner with silicon vendors, device manufacturers, and major app developers to influence Swift’s roadmaps and ensure low-friction adoption.
  • Segment Optimization: Build tailored product profiles and commercial requirements for both high-margin enterprise fleets (logistics, last-mile) and high-volume consumer mass-market devices.
  • GTM Collaboration: Support the Business Development lead on technical evaluation units, early pilots, and proofs-of-concept, and path to production with strategic global partners.
  • Market Defense: Maintain an aggressive feature roadmap that outpaces proprietary alternatives and establishes Swift as the platform-neutral benchmark.



Qualifications

  • Experience: 7+ years of product management experience defining and shipping platform, deep-tech, or developer-facing products within the mobile or hardware landscape.
  • Domain Knowledge: Solid understanding of the mobile positioning stack, location-based services (LBS), GNSS/GPS fundamentals, and/or mobile platform location frameworks (Android/iOS APIs).
  • Ecosystem Fluency: Proven ability to navigate multi-sided markets, aligning incentives between chip design, hardware manufacturing, and app development.
  • Core Skills: Excellent communication skills to bridge deep technical constraints with business strategy; comfortable with ambiguity and "0-to-1" product exploration.



Perks

  • Ability to obtain a TS/SCI security clearance.

  • Professional experience with DevOps practices, Jenkins, and continuous integration tools.
  • Professional experience working with Versal, MicroBlaze, bare metal development, and kernel/device drivers.

  • Experience in Command & Control Software, Sensor Processing Systems, and Optical Systems/telescopes.

title: Compliance Director
description:
The Compliance Director is responsible for building and managing the Bank’s compliance management system, owning OCC examination preparation and execution, and ensuring the Bank’s products, operations, and growth activities remain within regulatory requirements. This individual must be equally comfortable in digital banking and traditional branch environments, capable of navigating regulatory ambiguity without the luxury of large compliance teams, and skilled at leveraging technology, including AI tools, to operate with the efficiency a dynamic, growth-stage institution demands.

This is a senior individual contributor role. The successful candidate brings deep compliance expertise, strong independent judgment, and the ability to drive outcomes without organizational infrastructure around them.

Responsibilities

  • Manage examination timelines, information requests, and response quality across all examination types

  • Maintain and mature the Bank’s compliance management system within the three-lines-of-defense framework

  • Own the Bank’s compliance risk assessment, policy library, and annual compliance testing calendar

  • Ensure compliance program coverage across all BHC products, including digital and traditional banking, commercial lending, third-party partner services, bank-servicing, and branch operations

  • Coordinate with the designated BSA Officer on BSA/AML program alignment, maintaining clear lanes of ownership between compliance and AML functions

  • Lead the Bank’s fair lending program, including HMDA, ECOA, and fair lending risk assessment

  • Own CRA program administration, including CRA plan, data integrity, and examination readiness

  • Manage deposit operations compliance across digital and branch channels, including Regulation E, Regulation DD, bank-servicing, and applicable consumer protection requirements

  • Support planned product expansions (collateralized consumer lending, IRA trustee services) with regulatory analysis and compliance build-out

  • Provide compliance oversight for C&I and CRE lending activities, including adherence to applicable lending laws and OCC guidance

  • Partner with credit and operations teams on compliance requirements for commercial loan origination through servicing

  • Maintain compliance metrics, issue tracking, and management reporting in a form appropriate for OCC and Board review

  • Navigate regulatory ambiguity with a constructive, solutions-oriented approach - charting a defensible path forward rather than defaulting to prohibition

Salary range 160,000 - 195,000 USD

Required

  • 5-7 years of bank compliance experience, with meaningful exposure to OCC-supervised institutions

  • Demonstrated expertise in consumer compliance: fair lending, CRA, Regulation E, Regulation DD, and related consumer protection requirements

  • Direct experience with OCC examinations, including document production, examiner communication, and finding remediation

  • Working knowledge of operations compliance in both digital and traditional branch environments

  • Strong written communication skills - capable of producing examination responses, Board materials, and regulatory correspondence independently

  • Comfortable operating as an individual contributor in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment

  • Demonstrated ability to navigate regulatory ambiguity and develop practical, defensible compliance positions

Strongly Preferred

  • Demonstrated fluency with AI tools in a compliance context - regulatory research, policy drafting, exam preparation, monitoring, or documentation

  • Experience with digital banking products and platforms, including high-yield savings, consumer lending, mortgages, lending ratios, or payments

  • Familiarity with commercial lending compliance (C&I and/or CRE)

  • Experience in a fintech, holding company, or multi-entity regulated structure

  • BSA/AML familiarity sufficient to coordinate effectively with a designated BSA Officer

  • Experience with IRA trustee services compliance or collateralized consumer lending a plus

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree required

  • CRCM, CERP, or comparable compliance certification required

The right candidate is someone who has spent years inside regulated banking institutions, understands what OCC examiners look for, and knows how to build compliance infrastructure that holds up under scrutiny. They are equally capable in a branch environment and a digital one, not because they’ve done both simultaneously, but because they understand the distinct compliance demands of each and can bridge them.

Critically, this person is not a process-follower waiting for a rulebook. Regulatory ambiguity is a daily reality here. We need someone who can reason through an unsettled question, document their analysis, and move the institution forward with a defensible position.

Finally, this role rewards efficiency. The candidate who thrives here is one who embraces modern tools, including AI, as force multipliers, not as threats to the craft. The ability to produce high-quality compliance work with lean resources is both a requirement and a differentiator.

M1 is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity across the company. M1 does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Overview

The Retail Finance Senior Specialist supports the financing experience for customers purchasing vehicles through a direct-to-consumer sales model. This role helps manage loan and lease origination processes, ensures compliance with financing policies and regulations, partners with the internal delivery team, and works closely with captive finance partners to deliver a seamless customer experience.

description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Customer Experience Coordinator, your job is to define the customer’s experience through service, focus, and participation—so you are passionate about perfecting the experience before, during, and after their time at VEG. Outgoing and personable, with each customer, you conduct yourself professionally in both demeanor and presence. You find ways to say YES and put pets and customers experience above all else. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to grow where you want to go, building valuable experience and paving the way for your career to take unexpected and rewarding directions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Greet every customer with warmth and urgency, whether in person, over the phone, or online
  • Oversee all customer communications (calls, emails, texts), record details accurately, and route urgent medical calls to a doctor quickly
  • Deliver personalized, memorable experiences—always looking for creative ways to say “yes” to customer needs
  • Listen with empathy, resolve concerns quickly, and anticipate issues before they escalate
  • Keep nursing team and doctors updated on customer needs for a seamless care experience.
  • Provide confidential, compassionate guidance on financial options and end-of-life decisions
  • Process payments accurately while protecting personal and financial information.
  • Follow up with customers after visits to check on their pet’s care and strengthen relationships
  • Celebrate and capture special moments (with permission), creating lasting connections between customers, their pets, and the hospital

WHAT YOU NEED

  • 2+ years of experience in a customer service role
  • Advanced proficiency in computer programs and practice management software
  • Highly organized, with strong attention to detail
  • Strong communication skills; able to interact positively with anyone and everyone
  • The ability to multitask and thrive amid chaos
  • High emotional intelligence, able to read a room and plan and act accordingly
  • Adaptable and amenable in high stakes environments
  • Problem solving skills and a focus on innovation
  • Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors
  • Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs
  • Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

  • Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives
  • Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments
  • Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results
  • Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

  • Competitive compensation: pay range is $20-$30 and based on experience
  • A BIG focus on learning and growth from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to Unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (No really!). Part-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend. Part-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $400/year travel stipend.
  • Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work
  • Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people
  • And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

title: BOH Porter
description:
Description

esmero is looking for a full-time BOH Porter to join our team! The Polisher is a crucial part of the team to ensure high standards of sanitation and cleanliness for our guests. This is a full-time position, paid hourly, and candidates must be willing to work 40+ hours, 5 days a week (Wednesday - Sunday).

The name esmero embodies our purpose. It speaks to care, intention, and uncompromising attention to detail. Every gesture—whether sourcing an ingredient or a dish’s presentation—is guided by the pursuit of excellence and genuine hospitality.

Our ambition is not to redefine Mexican cuisine, but to contribute to its continuing story. To honor its past while embracing its future.

Led by Chef Adair Canacasco, esmero is the culmination of a lifelong exploration of Mexican identity, memory, and craftsmanship. Born in Mexico City and raised in the American Midwest, Chef Adair brings together heritage and contemporary technique through a collaborative creative process rooted in curiosity, discipline, and intention. Each course is thoughtfully composed to engage every sense, transforming familiar flavors into experiences that evoke emotion, inspire conversation, and create lasting memories.

Responsibilities

  • Wash dishes, glasses, pots and pans by hand or via commercial dish/glass washer

  • Quickly and safely polishing a wide variety of glassware

  • The ability to go up and down stairs with glassware trays

  • Dry and polish all serviceware, glassware and flatware

  • Maintaining the restrooms in service (guest and staff)

  • Breaking down stations at the end of service.

  • Report any maintenance deficiencies to appropriate resource

  • Sweep and mop floors, vacuum carpets

  • Removal of garbage and waste to compactors or recycling bins

  • Maintain general cleanliness of dining rooms, kitchens, restrooms and outside areas

  • Other duties as assigned by management

Requirements

  • 1 or more year experience of dishwashing or comparable position

  • Ability to operate dish machines, cleaning tools and other required equipment safely

  • Ability to follow instructions, anticipate needs, and multitask

  • Can work individually and within a team environment

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to work on your feet for at least 8 hours

  • Must be able to move, pull or lift at least 35 pounds

  • Must be able to climb stairs multiple times per shift

Benefits

  • Competitive hourly wage at $20.00 - $20.50/hour

  • Medical, vision, dental and life benefits available on the 1st month following full-time employment

    • 50% company contribution to single HMO during the first 2 years of full-time employment, 100% contribution available after 2 years

  • Paid time off

  • 401(K) with a company match of up to 4% of deferred earnings

  • CTA/Ventra discount available after 1 month of full-time employment

  • Employee Dining Discount, 20% to any Alinea Group restaurant

  • Referral Bonus Program available

The Alinea Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity in gender, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, religion, age, veteran status, life experiences and ideas. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities and strive to provide an inclusive culture that embraces diversity.

Must be eligible to legally work in the United States. We use E-Verify.

title: Finance & Business Management - Vice President
description:
Join the Commercial Bank’s Specialized Industries Business Management team as a Vice President, where you’ll provide strategic and tactical leverage to business leaders, enabling them to efficiently grow their segments, optimize bottom line performance, and meet the organization’s priorities and goals.

Commercial Banking is focused on helping our clients succeed and making a positive difference in our communities. We provide credit and financing, treasury and payment services, international banking and real estate services to clients including corporations, municipalities, institutions, real estate investors and owners, and nonprofit organizations. The Commercial Banking Specialized Industries business segment is a sector-driven group that delivers tailored solutions to clients across 20+ complex industries (including Healthcare, Multinational Corporations, Consumer, etc.).

As a Vice President within the Commercial Bank’s Specialized Industries Business Management team, you will play a pivotal role in this rapidly growing business focused on strategic projects critical to future growth. On our dynamic Specialized Industries team, you will apply your strategic vision and influence to collaborate with internal stakeholders and forward business goals. If you're ready to make an impact and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we want to hear from you!

Job responsibilities

  • Lead and support strategic initiatives within assigned focus areas of the Specialized Industries through active collaboration with Industry Managers.
  • Provide business insights through data-driven trend analysis with effective storytelling, message clarity, and analysis visualization to optimize performance and achieve Specialized Industries growth objectives.
  • Communicate key business metrics and their importance, both financial and non-financial, to support data-driven decision-making.
  • Apply strategic thought leadership skills to spearhead initiatives, develop business cases, and evaluate potential new opportunities aligned to senior leader priorities.
  • Respond promptly to executive requests, delivering high-quality program management, presentation development, and business analysis.
  • Collaborate with internal partners to enhance products and streamline processes impacting the sales organization.
  • Communicate effectively with key business partners to understand projects and forward next steps through effective project management.
  • Identify key business risks and forward resolution of mitigating controls.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or other related area.
  • At least 7 years of experience in business management, management consulting, or chief of staff roles.
  • Advanced analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data and provide actionable insights.
  • Proficiency in software and digital tools such as MS Office (PowerPoint and Excel), analytics automation platforms (e.g., Alteryx), and business intelligence/data visualization tools (e.g., Qlik).
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to convey complex information clearly.
  • Proven experience delivering timely, high-quality presentations and/or reporting for various projects and stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated intellectual curiosity and a proactive approach to learning and problem-solving , with a focus on innovative thinking and promoting change to achieve strategic goals.
  • Proven ability to effectively engage with diverse stakeholder groups, leveraging advanced communication skills to inspire collaboration and forward initiatives that achieve strategic objectives.
  • Demonstrated capability to navigate and clarify ambiguous requests, effectively managing upward relationships to ensure strategic alignment and structured execution.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Advanced organizational skills with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

  • Experience with commercial banking products and services and an understanding of the relevant financial metrics and performance indicators in the sector.
  • Knowledge of project management methodologies and tools.
  • Experience developing and implementing data infrastructure solutions for business management, reporting, or intelligence purposes.
  • Ability to quickly adapt to new technologies and tools in a fast-paced environment.

To be eligible for this role, you must be authorized to work in the United States. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this role. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase & Co. will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT).

title: Data Steward, Assistant Vice President
description:
Role Summary

The Data Steward serves as the primary execution lead for data governance and data quality oversight activities within across Markets business domains. The role partners with the Chief Data Office (CDO), Business Data Owners (BDOs), Global Critical Report and Key Metric Owners, Data Governance Leads, Technology stakeholders, Business Risk Management, and Data Consumers to support the governance, documentation, traceability, and oversight of data in accordance with the Global Data Governance Policy and related standards.

The role is responsible for maintaining catalog metadata, supporting data quality oversight processes, facilitating error resolution, and ensuring governance requirements are executed. The individual is also expected to interact and understand the multiple businesses across Markets and become a subject matter expert (SME) in the business and downstream use of data to ensure there is clear understanding of the impact on changes to data and the controls needed on data to mitigate data errors.

What You Will Be Responsible For

  • Execute data stewardship responsibilities for assigned business applications, datasets, EUDTs, and associated data assets, with priority focus on data supporting Critical Reports, Key Metrics, material legal entity obligations, and other functions with heightened regulatory oversight.

  • Drive the execution and maintenance of the business data dictionary, ensuring alignment with the enterprise glossary and that business definitions, data context, and usage requirements are clearly documented and understood

  • Coordinate metadata discovery, lineage updates, catalog remediation activities, and implementation of governance requirements resulting from application releases, architecture changes, remediation initiatives, or enterprise guidance updates.

  • Validate that end-to-end lineage for Critical Data Elements is documented, complete, and accurately reflects data capture, transformation, aggregation, consumption, reporting, and distribution processes.

  • Ensure business data definitions are appropriately mapped to technical metadata, physical data assets, and system objects within the Enterprise Data Governance Catalog.

  • Support the development, maintenance, and annual review of Data Provider/Consumer Agreements by coordinating with Data Providers, Data Consumers, Business Data Owners, and Critical Report/Key Metric Owners to document data quality requirements, timeliness expectations, materiality thresholds, and agreed escalation paths.

  • Maintain Data Quality Rules, Data Quality Controls, CDE metadata, report and metric associations, and governance relationships in the Enterprise Data Governance Catalog to ensure traceability and regulatory transparency

  • Maintain associations between Data Quality Rules, Data Quality Controls, CDEs, datasets, processes, reports, lineage assets, and applicable Data Quality Dimensions.

  • Log, track, and facilitate investigation of Data Quality Exceptions; coordinate root-cause analysis and remediation activities across business, operations, and technology stakeholders. Escalate recurring or control-related concerns for Data Quality Issue evaluation when appropriate.

  • Support and facilitate periodic governance reviews and certifications

  • Represent the business area in Data Steward communities, working groups, and governance initiatives, helping drive adoption of enterprise standards and best practices.

What We Value

The following skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Strong understanding of financial services, trading, brokerage, banking, operational processes, and the data that supports those activities.

  • Experience with data governance, data stewardship, metadata management, data quality management, data lineage, or related data management disciplines.

  • Experience maintaining governance metadata and lineage within enterprise data catalog platforms such as Collibra or similar governance tooling.

  • Ability to influence and collaborate with business, technology, risk, operations, and governance stakeholders across a matrixed organization.

  • Strong understanding of data models, data standards, data taxonomy, authoritative sourcing, lineage concepts, and governance controls.

  • Experience supporting data quality investigations, root-cause analysis, exception management, remediation tracking, and issue escalation.

  • Ability to manage competing priorities while delivering accurate, timely, and sustainable governance outcomes.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, written communication, verbal communication, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Familiarity with regulatory data governance expectations, BCBS 239 principles, critical information governance, and enterprise risk management practices is desirable.

AVP Accountability Statement

Acts as the primary execution lead for data governance and data stewardship activities within the assigned business domain. Responsible for maintaining accurate and complete metadata, Critical Data Element documentation, lineage, Data Quality Rule and Control traceability, data quality error oversight, and governance reporting inputs. Drives adherence to enterprise standards, supports implementation of data quality management requirements, facilitates issue resolution and remediation tracking, and promotes transparency of data assets, lineage, controls, and risks. Escalates material governance, lineage, and data quality concerns through established governance channels while reinforcing Business Data Owner accountability for data quality outcomes, control ownership, and risk management

$90,000 - $142,500 Annual

title: Regional Business Director, Mountain West
description:
MISSION

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Regional Business Director (RBD) is a first-line field leader responsible for leading, coaching, and developing a team of (7) Regional Account Managers to deliver strong, sustainable business performance and meaningful patient impact across an assigned region. The RBD translates national and zone strategy into focused local execution, builds a culture of continuous learning and accountability, and ensures the team operates with clinical credibility, business discipline, and a deep commitment to patients and caregivers.

This leader will create clarity in a complex rare disease environment, set high standards for execution, and develop talent through frequent field coaching, timely feedback, individualized development plans, and stretch opportunities. The RBD will also serve as a trusted cross-functional partner, bringing forward actionable field insights and aligning Marketing, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, and Advocacy around the needs of customers, patients, and the business.

Assigned Area: CO, UT, OR, WA, AZ

JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Regional Strategy & Performance Leadership

  • Translate national and zone priorities into a focused regional business plan with clear objectives, account priorities, resource allocation, and measures of success.
  • Set a disciplined operating rhythm that includes field coaching, business reviews, performance tracking, opportunity planning, and rapid course correction.
  • Use data, market intelligence, and field insights to identify growth opportunities, anticipate barriers, and improve execution across the region.
  • Own regional results and resource stewardship, including budget management, forecasting, and alignment of team activity to the highest-impact opportunities.

People Leadership, Coaching & Development

  • Recruit, onboard, develop, engage, and retain high-performing Regional Account Managers who demonstrate strong clinical credibility, business judgment, and patient focus.
  • Spend meaningful time in the field observing customer engagement, coaching in the moment, reinforcing strengths, and addressing capability gaps through clear, actionable feedback.
  • Create individualized development plans, provide stretch opportunities, and build succession and promotion readiness across the team.
  • Set clear expectations and hold self and team accountable for behaviors, execution quality, and results; address performance concerns promptly, consistently, and fairly.

Customer, Account & Patient Impact

  • Ensure the team develops thoughtful account strategies that reflect local patient journeys, referral networks, access dynamics, customer needs, and competitive realities.
  • Raise the quality and consistency of customer engagement across pediatric and adult hepatology and gastroenterology settings, including priority systems and centers of excellence.
  • Support compliant coordination across field partners to help remove appropriate barriers in the patient journey from identification through treatment initiation and persistence.
  • Promote a customer’s experience grounded in trust, empathy, responsiveness, and follow-through with healthcare professionals, and care teams.

Clinical & Business Acumen

  • Build a team that can confidently bridge science and strategy in a high-science rare disease market.
  • Maintain strong knowledge of rare cholestatic liver disease, the Liver portfolio, market dynamics, patient support pathways, access and reimbursement, and the evolving competitive landscape.
  • Coach the team to communicate with clinical relevance, ask insightful questions, challenge constructively, and tailor engagement to the needs of each customer and account.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Build trusted partnerships across Marketing, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, Analytics, and Advocacy.
  • Bring forward timely, objective, and actionable field insights that inform strategy, messaging, training, resource development, and execution priorities.
  • Align cross-functional partners around regional opportunities and barriers, clarify ownership, and ensure consistent follow-through on agreed actions.

Culture, Change & Compliance

  • Lead with humility, transparency, optimism, and consistency; create a safe, inclusive environment where people can learn, contribute, and perform at their best.
  • Champion change, simplify complexity, remove obstacles, and help the team remain focused and resilient amid ambiguity and evolving business needs.
  • Model and reinforce the highest standards of ethical conduct and compliance with all laws, regulations, company policies, and approved promotional practices.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
  • 10+ years of progressive commercial experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
  • 3+ years of successful first-line sales leadership experience with direct responsibility for field team performance and talent development.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering business results while building engaged, capable, and accountable teams.
  • Strong experience coaching in the field, providing candid and constructive feedback, managing performance, and developing future leaders.
  • Rare disease, orphan drug, or highly specialized high-science commercial experience.
  • Experience in hepatology, gastroenterology, pediatric specialty care, or other complex specialty markets.
  • Experience leading through launch, indication expansion, organizational change, or a dynamic competitive market.
  • Knowledge of account-based selling, health-system dynamics, referral networks, centers of excellence and the role of patient services in rare disease markets
  • Experience partnering closely with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, and Operations.
  • Ability to interpret business data, identify insights, develop regional strategies, and translate plans into consistent field execution.
  • Excellent communication, executive presence, judgment, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize in a fast-moving environment.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel up to 70%, including frequent overnight travel and occasional weekend commitments.

#LI-REMOTE

title: Regional Director, Manhattan
description:
At BBYO, we’re motivated by our mission, inspiring us to reimagine work to make it fun, flexible, and fulfilling. We are looking for a passionate Regional Director to join our Manhattan BBYO team and make a difference. As a Regional Director, you’ll play a pivotal role in growing membership, training regional and chapter teen leaders, deepening support for BBYO in the Manhattan community, and leading organization-wide initiatives that produce meaningful, Jewish experiences for Jewish teens. Alongside your team, you’ll connect in a dynamic environment and create a positive impact on teens, our community, and the world.

SHAPING THE FUTURE FOR TEENS AND YOURSELF

As a Regional Director, a typical day will include:

  • Developing regional vision and strategy to drive membership growth, strengthen chapters, and expand BBYO's impact across Manhattan & the Bronx
  • Expanding BBYO's presence across New York City by cultivating community partnerships and leading collaborative events and city-wide initiatives
  • Planning and executing high-impact programs, community initiatives, and two annual overnight conventions from start to finish
  • Building a strong and connected BBYO community by fostering belonging, strengthening relationships, and creating meaningful opportunities for teens, advisors, and families to engage
  • Coaching teen leaders through conflict resolution, democratic leadership, and project management to expand membership, deepen engagement, and strengthen leadership pipelines
  • Recruiting, training, placing, and supporting volunteer advisors through ongoing guidance, supervision, and appreciation
  • Attending summer camp (but this time you’re in charge!) as you lead teen leadership programs
  • Empowering and inspiring staff, teens, volunteers and advisors through your mentorship, coaching and training

ESSENTIAL SKILLS FOR MAKING A LASTING IMPACT

Our team has an entrepreneurial spirit and a passion for innovation to drive positive change. Additionally, as a Regional Director, these skills are key to success:

  • Abilities: Experience working with youth or teens is preferred; ability to manage event logistics and perform physical tasks, including lifting and carrying up to 50 pounds, as needed
  • Experience: 3-5 years of professional work experience, preferably in youth development, community building, education, nonprofit, or related fields
  • Education: Bachelor's degree or higher
  • Location: Must reside in Manhattan or be willing to relocate to Manhattan

REQUIREMENTS

  • Attend all regional conventions and major events including Staff Conference, and International Convention each year.
  • Ability to travel as needed and to staff a summer leadership program for 2-3 weeks during summer
  • Unrestricted authorization to work in the U.S. without holding a visa or sponsorship.
  • To perform this job successfully, the individual must be able to perform each essential duty/function with or without reasonable accommodation in accordance with applicable law.
  • Ability to have access to reliable transportation, whether via personal vehicle or public transit, to ensure timely arrival at events

BENEFITS OF OUR DYNAMIC AND SUPPORTIVE WORKPLACE

Own Your Balance

  • Flexible work environment
  • Unlimited paid time off (PTO)
  • 18 paid secular and Jewish holidays
  • PLUStwo-week long office shutdowns

Invest in Your Well-being

  • Medical, dental, vision, short- & long-term disability, and 2.5x salary life insurance
  • Generous 403b and Roth retirement plan with vested match
  • Free access toWellHub, which includes access to gyms, onlineworkouts and wellness apps

Family First Environment

  • Teen Involvement Benefit stipend
  • Flexibility in bringing child(ren) on business travel
  • Generous paid parental leave

Salary Range: $72,000 - $76,000. This position is eligible for a discretionary bonus incentive based on individual performance.

We also pay for your TSA pre-check, provide a home technology allowance and have pet insurance options!

BE APART OF A LEGACY...

  • that celebrates our rich, century-long history of enhancing the Jewish experience to build a meaningful, teen-led future
  • with an inclusive culture where authenticity is celebrated, respect is given, and fun is encouraged
  • built on trust and empowerment, offering flexibility in where you work and autonomy in how it gets done

Embracing our past and future, we are excited about our growth and the challenges ahead. Join us and embark on an exciting journey with BBYO. INSPIRING TODAY. BUILDING TOMORROW.

title: Retail Receiving & Stock Associate -  PT
description:

title: Therapeutic Recovery Coach
description:
Position: Therapeutic Recovery Coach
Location: Chicago, IL
Status: Part-Time, PRN (per circumstance and as needed),

Compensation Scale:
Bachelors - $25 - $70
Masters - $70 - $135
PhD/Doctorate - $130 - $165
Final rate of pay may vary from the above based on experience and skill set and will be mutually agreed upon during the interview process.


Who We Are:

Intent Clinical offers a continuum of services to guide individuals and families through the behavioral health industry by providing concierge-level care, identifying suitable treatment and aftercare options, and assist in creating and implementing sustainable recovery plans. We help address the needs of those struggling with behavioral health issues including substance use disorders, mental health issues, eating disorders, and mood and personality disorders. We also support individuals on the autism spectrum, aging adults with dementia, and young adults who are struggling with transitions to independence.


Who you are:

You are professional, dependable, and able to tailor your therapeutic approach according to each client’s specific needs. You are knowledgeable about clinical mental health diagnosis and have client-facing behavioral health experience. You are dedicated to the client’s well-being, understand the importance of confidentiality and discretion, and are adept at managing crises while remaining calm and focused. You are comfortable with a flexible work schedule and being assigned cases on an as-needed basis. The ideal case management/recovery coach candidate is adept at working independently while also thriving with supervision and guidance.

What You’ll Do:
  • Participating in initial consults and writing corresponding consult reports.
  • Completing biopsychosocial assessments on clients.
  • Reviewing past treatment records and contacting clinical providers.
  • Coordinating and helping to complete a comprehensive consultation addressing the client’s educational, vocational, recreational, and social needs.
  • Clinical: defining what clinical services will be accessed and how frequently. Facilitating efficient communication between treatment team, client, and family coach.
  • Educational: assistance in selecting a school program. Supporting a client’s school plan, including class selection, connections, and school-based resources (i.e. tutoring and counseling).
  • Vocational plan: assessment of vocational interests, short-term support for finding and keeping a job and long-term planning towards career goals.
  • Recreational plan: discovery of clients’ interests in cultural, sports-related, and artistic pursuits. Connections to appropriate resources.
  • Social: developing skills to pursue healthy behaviors and assistance in cultivating a positive support network.
  • Independent living skills: creation and monitoring of a budget, assistance with time management and other basic living skills as needed.
  • Creating short and long-term client goal plans; daily documenting of progress.
  • Meeting with client 1-5 times per week in the community or home settings to monitor client progress, with follow up calls as appropriate.
  • Providing connections to endorse community resources, treatment options, peer counselors and AA companions as appropriate.
  • Providing observed in-home drug testing and Soberlink monitoring if appropriate
  • Emergency support, on-call availability, and client transportation as needed.
  • Additional duties will be assigned as deemed appropriate.

What you’ll bring:
  • One year or more of direct client experience in behavioral health or related fields
  • Experience supporting clients with thought disorders, schizoaffective disorders or related symptoms
  • Minimum of a Bachelor's Degree or equivalent
  • Ability to calmly, flexibly, and efficiently manage client crises as they arise
  • Valid driver’s license with safe driving record
  • Ability to work collaboratively as well as independently
  • Knowledge of mental health diagnoses and behavioral health treatments
  • Comfort and quick learning curve with technology on day-to-day tasks (i.e. Microsoft Office, Salesforce)

You ideally have (but not required):
  • Experience working as a recovery coach, mental health clinician or therapeutic companion
  • Working knowledge of men's mental health challenges
  • Experience working with high-net worth families
  • Professional licensure (i.e. LMSW, LMHC, LMFT)
  • Demonstrated engagement in community service initiatives, particularly those focused on underserved communities
  • An understanding of social responsibility and how to contribute positively to the well-being of others


What we'll bring:
  • A collaborative and supportive culture focused on your personal and professional growth.
  • Weekly supervision with your supervisor.
  • 24/7 access to clinical support while on a case.
  • Regular paid professional development meetings covering a variety of professionally relevant topics.
  • Flexible Schedule

This position is part-time and per circumstance only, and hours are not guaranteed per week. Case Managers/Recovery Coaches on our staff list are contacted on an as-needed basis for cases as they arise.

title: SAP MDG Technical Developer
description:
C5MI is not your typical consulting firm. We are a high-performance team of SAP and supply chain experts who solve complex, mission critical challenges for organizations that cannot afford failure.

We hire consultants who thrive in complexity, move fast, take ownership, and deliver under pressure. At C5MI, you will not be siloed or stuck in theory. You will be hands on, client facing, and directly influencing outcomes that matter.

Our culture rewards initiative, accountability, and continuous growth. This is a place where your expertise is valued, your work is meaningful, and your performance truly matters. If you’re energized by learning through real-world challenges, collaborating with top-tier talent, and expanding your capabilities every day, C5MI is where strong consultants level up.

Position Summary:

The SAP MDG Technical Developer is responsible for designing, developing, configuring, and supporting SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) technical solutions within a federal SAP S/4HANA environment. This role collaborates with government stakeholders, functional consultants, architects, and technical teams to develop scalable master data governance solutions that support enterprise data quality, workflow automation, and system integration. The developer leverages expertise in SAP MDG, Object-Oriented ABAP, SAP Fiori, BRF+, and SAP development frameworks to deliver custom enhancements, workflows, interfaces, and data replication capabilities that support enterprise master data initiatives.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and enhance SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) technical solutions supporting enterprise master data governance initiatives.
  • Develop custom applications, enhancements, and technical objects using Object-Oriented ABAP, ABAP Managed Database Procedures (AMDP), CDS Views, and SAP development best practices.
  • Configure and develop Business Rule Framework Plus (BRF+) applications, decision tables, validation rules, derivation rules, and business rule services.
  • Design, develop, and maintain SAP MDG workflows, including single-step, multi-step, sequential, and parallel approval workflows.
  • Develop and enhance SAP MDG user interfaces utilizing Floorplan Manager (FPM), SAP Fiori, Web Dynpro, OData Services, and related SAP UI technologies.
  • Configure and support the Data Replication Framework (DRF) and Data Import Framework (DIF) to synchronize master data across SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, and integrated third-party systems.
  • Develop inbound and outbound interfaces utilizing IDocs, SOA Services, Web Services, APIs, and enterprise integration technologies.
  • Collaborate with functional consultants to translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions.
  • Develop technical specifications and support functional design documentation.
  • Perform technical unit testing, integration testing, code reviews, and defect resolution activities.
  • Support data migration, conversion, and enterprise master data implementation activities.
  • Troubleshoot production issues, optimize application performance, and support ongoing system enhancements.
  • Participate in Agile development activities, sprint planning, code management, and DevOps processes.
  • Travel on rare occasions to client sites to provide on-site support.
  • Adhere to all certified processes as part of our commitment to maintaining the highest standards of quality and information security, including actively participating in quality assurance activities and ensuring the protection of sensitive information in accordance with our security policies.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; 5+ years of SAP development experience with demonstrated expertise in SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) technical development (5–7 years without a Bachelor’s degree).
  • Demonstrated experience developing SAP MDG technical solutions using Object-Oriented ABAP, BRF+, SAP Fiori, Floorplan Manager (FPM), Web Dynpro, OData Services, CDS Views, and ABAP Managed Database Procedures (AMDP).
  • Experience configuring SAP MDG workflows, data models, validation rules, derivation rules, and business rule frameworks.
  • Experience configuring and supporting the SAP Data Replication Framework (DRF), Data Import Framework (DIF), and enterprise integration technologies including IDocs, SOA Services, Web Services, and APIs.
  • Strong understanding of SAP MDG architecture, Central Governance, Mass Processing, and Data Quality Management (DQM).
  • Experience supporting one or more SAP master data domains, including Business Partner, Customer, Supplier, Material Master, or Financial Master Data.
  • Experience supporting SAP S/4HANA implementations, upgrades, or enterprise modernization initiatives.
  • Experience gathering technical requirements, developing technical specifications, and supporting solution delivery.
  • Ability to exercise judgment within defined practices and resolve moderately complex SAP MDG technical issues with minimal oversight.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain an active Secret security clearance (requires U.S. citizenship).

Nice to Have:

  • Active Secret security clearance.
  • Experience supporting SAP S/4HANA implementations, federal ERP modernization programs, or Department of Defense (DoD) SAP environments.
  • Experience with SAP Activate methodology, Agile (Scrum), DevOps practices, JIRA, ATC checks, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience developing SAP Fiori applications and OData Services.
  • Experience integrating SAP MDG with SAP ECC, SAP S/4HANA, and third-party enterprise applications.
  • Relevant SAP MDG, SAP ABAP, SAP Fiori, or SAP S/4HANA certifications.

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Who is Aiwyn and what do we do?

Aiwyn is the first complete platform for modern Accounting Firms. Backed by top-tier investors like Bessemer, KKR, and Revolution, we’re one of the fastest-growing scale-up SaaS companies in the world. We build category-defining technology—and we’re doing it with world-class people, processes, and products.

To learn more, visit our website

Role Overview:

Our Design org sits at an inflection point: as our product surface area grows across business lines, we need designers who can operate above any single team and shape how our platform coheres as a whole.

For Staff-level roles at Aiwyn, focus shifts based on where design has the greatest impact. This role begins with a clear mandate: preparing our design system to support AI-driven prototyping and development. As AI tools take on more of the work of generating and modifying interfaces, they depend on a system that's consistent and well-structured underneath. Your initial focus will be building that foundation.

As the system matures, we'll assess where your focus can add the most value going forward. That may mean continuing to lead the system, or shifting toward a specific product area while staying connected to its direction.

Who Are You?

You're in the top tier of your craft, the kind of talent that's shaped product at companies where design is a genuine competitive differentiator, not just a support function. You've spent years solving complex B2B problems, and you've learned that the highest-leverage work often isn't the next feature. It's the underlying patterns, components, and standards that make every future feature faster and more consistent to ship, and it's also the last mile of polish that makes something feel magical rather than merely functional.

You operate with real autonomy in ambiguous situations. You don't wait for a brief; you figure out what needs to be done, make the case for it, and own the outcome, not just the mocks you produced. You care about the people around you as much as the pixels. You mentor generously, give feedback that lands, and help other designers see problems more clearly.

What Makes This Role Unique:

Design at Aiwyn increasingly sits at the intersection of craft and AI-assisted workflows. Our design system is what lets that scale: the mechanism that allows engineers and AI to produce on-system UI without a designer touching every screen. Strengthening it is how product quality scales without just adding headcount, and this role puts you at the center of that shift early.

At the same time, this isn't a purely systems role. You'll lead design on complex initiatives across product teams, hold the quality bar for the surfaces you own, and represent design's point of view directly to product and engineering leadership.

Key Responsibilities

  • Quality Bar: Define what "great" looks like for the surfaces you own — not just functional, but the kind of synthesis that makes something feel magical. Build standards and systems that hold that bar even as AI generates more of the UI, so quality doesn't depend on you personally reviewing every screen.

  • Design System Stewardship: Drive the strategic direction, quality, and consistency of our design system. Identify gaps across business lines, advocate for system investment, and support adoption through AI enablement.

  • Strategy & Vision: Contribute directly to product strategy and drive product vision in partnership with product leads. Bring a first-principles lens to the biggest, most ambiguous problems.

  • Complex System Design: Solve system-level design challenges—the kind that touch information architecture, shared components, and cross-surface consistency.

  • Research Leadership: Lead quantitative and qualitative research efforts that inform decisions across your product area, not just a single feature.

  • Mentorship & Guild Leadership: Coach and grow other designers. Actively lead initiatives, design reviews, and process improvements that raise the bar for the whole team.
